newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end up, helped by housing data.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end up, helped by housing data.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Tuesday, helped by some year-end fund short covering, against the background of higher-than-expected US November housing starts, traders said.

"Silver looks like it might have more upside potential, but overall today's action was probably just a blip up caused by fund short covering and the big housing starts number," Linnco Futures Group's Chicago trader Anthony Raia said.
U.S. November housing starts were 1.415 million at an annual rate, up 9.2 percent, the biggest monthly rise since July 1995.
But the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, as expected, seeing little evidence of inflation.
COMEX February gold closed up 60 cents at $370.50 an ounce, but failed to clear resistance around $372.00.
Estimated gold futures volume was 37,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.40/368.80, up from the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $368.20, and the New York close Monday at $367.80/368.30.
Further weakness in U.S. bond and stock markets early Tuesday also helped provide some support, but near the close U.S. equity markets were steady.
Precious metals have been consolidating in the past 10 days after spot gold slid to a three year low at $366.00 an ounce at the end of November.
"Interim support remains at $367 an ounce in February gold, with a major technical target of $364 on the downside," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.

"A sell off to those levels cannot be ruled out in the next week or two, but $364 appears to be a strong technical base and there has been evidence of some significant buying in Asia at prices below $370."
"If the market holds around $370, prices could stage a modest rebound."
The spot gold/silver ratio fell to two month lows at 75.95 Tuesday though, reflecting the relative strength in silver.
March silver ended up 5.8 cents at $4.893 an ounce, after seeing a 15-day intraday high at $4.955. Estimated silver volume was 16,000 lots.
NYMEX January platinum ended up $1.70 at $371.50 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed down 25 cents t $119.50.
The April platinum/gold spread was little changed at 70 cents an ounce, after dipping to zero and a two month low Monday.
